# Approach-direction leaf-interference study (SIMULATED)

> Rigid, fixed leaves from the procedural rosette model; butterhead near harvest (300 sampled plants with two same-channel neighbours each, seed 0). The metric is the share of leaf area inside the volume swept by the tool. It is an upper bound on contact and **not** a damage prediction.

| strategy | target plant: leaf area in tool path (mean / p95) | target inner leaves (heart) | neighbouring plants |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 top-down onto the stem (compact tool, vertical shank) | 75.8% / 85.2% | 97.7% / 100.0% | 0.0% / 0.0% |
| S2 descend through canopy beside the stem, short slide | 72.3% / 83.3% | 79.3% / 94.7% | 0.0% / 0.0% |
| S3 side entry under canopy (low-profile head on boom) | 28.6% / 38.0% | 1.0% / 3.6% | 0.0% / 0.0% |

Reading: with side entry the tool path contains only low outer leaves and essentially none of the heart, whereas descending through the canopy, at the stem or beside it, puts most of the leaf area, including the heart, in the tool's way. The conclusion rests on the assumed leaf geometry (flat elliptical leaves, assumed elevation angles) and must be re-checked against scans or photographs of real plants.
